rationale: W0 for farnesane (2,6,10-trimethyldodecane, a fuel of the Cool Flames Investigation, PSI-39), one shot for this fuel and not zero-shot: no farnesane outcome was opened, but the law is the n-heptane law of flex_heptane.wsp5, whose numbers were typed after the n-heptane train partition. The weakest of the carried-over candidates: density and a calculated boiling point come from commercial data sheets, the latent heat from Kistiakowsky's rule, and heat capacity, conductivity, heat of combustion and the density at boiling are estimates by analogy with n-dodecane. Each fuel-specific number is the n-heptane number times a ratio worked by hand from property values: the hot-flame level, its oxygen and pressure dependence and the heat-up from a transfer number that includes the heating of the liquid; the critical diameter of radiative extinction as the inverse of the mass burning flux; the cool-flame rate from the wet-bulb transfer number under a 700 K flame and its end diameter from an equal residence time; the unlit droplet as self-cooling evaporation with property constants. The oxygen limit of the cool flame (0.08 atm) is a judgement from one published cetane number. The forward has no reignition of the hot flame, no separate warm-flame stage, no direct cool ignition and no fibre, refuses above 4.4 atm and stops 45 s after ignition. The spreads are the widest of the set. Literal revision of the fuel's lineage root (the D^2-law reference of n-heptane, copied without change), not a root, because the author has seen other candidates; it writes every authored element, so nothing of the root survives. The parent id is a placeholder until the fuel is registered in droplet6.rs and the root is built: tools/wsp/reassemble.py then writes it. See docs/wsp/research/phys_droplet_fuels.md.
